summary:
Delaware is a state within the United States and stands under the national framework carried by the national record and the parent bundle; what follows is Delaware's own law and practice.

A national trans legal risk assessment dated July 2026 places Delaware in its Low-Risk States group, alongside Arizona, Maine, Michigan, Nevada, Pennsylvania, Virginia, Wisconsin and the District of Columbia, defined there as jurisdictions that largely refrain from targeting transgender adults without specialising in their protection.

Delaware has no ban on transgender people using public bathrooms and facilities according to their gender identity; the Movement Advancement Project equality map records no such restriction for the state.

Since 2013, under SB 97, Delaware prohibits discrimination on the basis of actual or perceived gender identity in employment, housing, public accommodations and other areas. The bill passed the Senate 11-7 on 6 June 2013, passed the House 24-17 with amendments, passed the Senate on amendments 11-9 on 18 June, was signed the next day and took effect immediately.

Since 2013 Delaware has imposed additional penalties for a violent crime motivated by the victim's actual or perceived gender identity.

HB142, which would formally repeal the common-law gay and trans panic defence and ban its use, was introduced in May 2023 and passed both houses of the Legislature in June 2023; the source records the Governor as having neither signed nor vetoed it.

Delaware allows a change of legal gender marker on state-issued identification on the signed statement of a licensed medical provider alone. Since 11 February 2017 sex reassignment surgery has not been an explicit requirement for an amended birth certificate, which instead requires a signed affidavit of surgical, hormonal, psychological or other treatment appropriate for gender transition. As of April 2020 Delaware did not offer a gender X marker on driver's licences.

Same-sex marriage has been legal since 1 July 2013, with civil unions converted to marriages.

State-level protection machinery includes an Executive Order of 11 August 2009 extending anti-discrimination safeguards to state employees and applicants on the basis of gender identity, and an Executive Order signed in January 2025 by Governor Hall-Long creating Delaware's LGBTQ+ Commission.
tangentialFactors:
The July 2026 assessment's own definition of the Low-Risk group is relative rather than protective: membership indicates that a state largely refrains from targeting transgender adults, not that it legislates affirmatively for them. Delaware's classification should be read against that wording.

Delaware's core protections date from 2013 and predate the current federal posture, so they operate as a state layer alongside national rules on travel documents and entry, which the parent record carries.

Two Delaware measures were unresolved at the time of sourcing: HB142 on the gay and trans panic defence, passed in June 2023 but recorded without executive action, and the gender X question on driver's licences, for which the inventory supplies only an April 2020 position.
localsOnly:
Delaware's anti-discrimination coverage of gender identity extends to employment, housing and public accommodations under SB 97, and an Executive Order of 11 August 2009 separately protects employees and applicants in state executive branch departments and agencies.

Since 26 March 2016 Delaware has prohibited discrimination based on gender identity within insurance contracts, including sex reassignment surgery.

SB 65, introduced 26 April 2017 and signed and effective 23 July 2018 as Laws of Delaware 81:340, defines conversion therapy to include practices seeking to change gender identity, behaviours or gender expressions, and makes it unprofessional conduct subject to discipline for physicians, nurses, mental health and chemical dependency professionals, psychologists and clinical social workers who perform it on a minor or refer a minor out of state for it; the Department of Services for Children, Youth and Their Families is barred from performing or recommending it for a minor.

A law signed 25 June 2015 and effective immediately allows inmates to access and change the name on birth certificates to reflect gender identity, where previously inmates could change names only for religious reasons.

Delaware's LGBTQ+ Commission was created by executive order in January 2025 under Governor Hall-Long.
outOfScopeNotes:
The Movement Advancement Project page on bathroom and facilities bans was not retrievable at the archived URL used (HTTP 404); the finding that Delaware has no such ban is carried from the underlying equality map rather than read off the page itself.

No Delaware-specific policy on the placement of transgender inmates in state custody is documented in the inventory; national corrections guidance on this question is carried by the parent record.

The status of HB142 after its passage in June 2023 is unresolved in the sources: no signature, veto or later disposition is recorded.

The absence of a gender X option on Delaware driver's licences is stated as of April 2020 and has not been verified as current.

The inventory supplies no Delaware figures on enforcement of the 2013 gender-identity penalty enhancement or on reported incidents of anti-trans violence in the state.
